intents.name: EVENT_OUTCOME_RESOLUTION
intents.description: Resolves objective real-world event outcomes for prediction markets and conditional contracts using quorum oracles.
intents.why: Settled outcome is checkable; pre-settlement resolution of ambiguous or disputed events is judgment.
intents.scale: Miners scrape consensus from 10+ independent news outlets, sports APIs, or flight statuses.

intents.name: WASH_TRADING_DETECTION
intents.description: Analyzes DEX transaction graphs and circular transfer loops between affiliated wallets to identify artificial trade volume.
intents.why: Circular-flow and address-identity checks are mechanical; intent to wash is inferred.
intents.scale: Miners run distinct graph-analysis heuristics across different indexed subgraphs.

intents.name: ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY
intents.description: Validates smart contract event logs, gas consumption, token balances, and wallet transaction states directly on-chain.
intents.why: Read a value from an RPC node at a block height.
intents.scale: Miners query independent RPC providers and archive nodes to prevent single-provider spoofing.

intents.name: LIQUIDITY_DEPTH_VERIFY
intents.description: Measures bid-ask order book depth, cumulative slippage bands, and market maker liquidity across decentralized pools.
intents.why: Orderbook depth at a timestamp is an observable number.
intents.scale: Miners query different decentralized exchange liquidity subgraphs and order books.

intents.name: CROSS_CHAIN_STATE_VERIFY
intents.description: Proves cryptographic Merkle-Patricia state roots and cross-chain message execution headers between distinct blockchain networks.
intents.why: Light-client proof either verifies or does not.
intents.scale: Miners independently verify state roots by querying different cross-chain relayer nodes.

intents.name: OPTIMAL_EXECUTION_ROUTE
intents.description: Determines optimal multi-venue order execution routing to minimize slippage, exchange fees, and market impact.
intents.why: Executed price is checkable; 'optimal' depends on an objective the request may not fix.
intents.scale: Miners query different DEX aggregators and private RPCs for the best routing path.

intents.name: CODE_REVIEW
intents.description: Evaluates source code pull requests against internal architectural patterns, maintainability standards, and syntax rules.
intents.why: No correct review exists; quality is comparative.
intents.scale: 10 miners use 10 different coding models to execute static analysis on the same GitHub PR.

intents.name: SECURITY_REVIEW
intents.description: Scans codebase dependencies, API endpoints, and configuration files for common CVEs, secrets leakage, and misconfigurations.
intents.why: Known-pattern findings are mechanical; severity and exploitability are judgment.
intents.scale: Miners scan the codebase using different open-source SCA/SAST vulnerability engines.
intents.verifyNote: Different SAST/SCA scanners return different findings on identical code; there is no single convergent finding set to check against.

intents.name: VULNERABILITY_TRIAGE
intents.description: Ranks and categorizes detected vulnerabilities by CVSS score, active exploit availability, and asset criticality.
intents.why: CVE lookup is a fact; priority ordering is judgment.
intents.scale: Miners cross-reference CVSS severity scores from different global vulnerability databases.

intents.name: CODE_PATCH_VERIFY
intents.description: Validates that software patch commits compile, resolve targeted defects, and introduce no regression side effects.
intents.why: Build and test suite pass or fail.
intents.scale: Miners run the patch in isolated sandbox environments to verify zero exit status.

intents.name: LIVE_SHELF_PRICE
intents.description: Fetches and verifies current live shelf or retail listing prices across online merchant catalogs and marketplaces.
intents.why: A quoted price at a moment, numeric tolerance.
intents.scale: Miners use different scraping endpoints to find the median price.

intents.name: SKU_IN_STOCK
intents.description: Confirms real-time stock availability, quantities, and warehouse fulfillment readiness for a given SKU.
intents.why: Boolean from an inventory system.
intents.scale: Miners use different proxy networks and inventory APIs to confirm stock booleans.

intents.name: COMMERCE_PURCHASE_VERIFY
intents.description: Verifies the authenticity, item line totals, and payment authorization for a completed e-commerce purchase transaction.
intents.why: Order exists in the merchant API or it does not.
intents.scale: Miners verify receipt hashes against payment webhook schemas.

intents.name: TRAVEL_DISRUPTION
intents.description: Detects and monitors flight delays, cancellations, gate shifts, and weather-driven travel disruptions in real time.
intents.why: Flight status from an FAA/telemetry feed.
intents.scale: Miners query independent aviation telemetry endpoints to verify ground stops and delays.

intents.name: ASSET_RESERVE_ATTESTATION
intents.description: Verifies cryptographic proof-of-reserves and custodial bank confirmations backing stablecoins and tokenized assets.
intents.why: Attested balance compared against a custody feed.
intents.scale: Miners cross-reference on-chain reserve wallet balances with custodian public API endpoints.

intents.name: SANCTIONS_SCREENING_MATCH
intents.description: Screens counterparties and beneficial owners against OFAC, EU, and UN consolidated financial sanctions lists.
intents.why: Exact list hits are mechanical; fuzzy name matching is judgment.
intents.scale: Miners use different matching algorithms (Levenshtein, Jaro-Winkler) against the OpenSanctions DB.

intents.name: KYC_BIOMETRIC_LIVENESS
intents.description: Verifies user selfie liveness video capture against government photo IDs to prevent spoofing fraud.
intents.why: Engine returns a score; the accept/reject boundary and spoof reasoning are judgment.
intents.scale: Miners run distinct computer-vision liveness verification models.
intents.verifyNote: Ground truth is private user data plus an engine-specific liveness score; it cannot be made public or replicated.

intents.name: PAYMENT_METHOD_VERIFY
intents.description: Verifies card BIN validity, tokenization credentials, bank account routing, and active account standing.
intents.why: Bank switch returns a definitive validity response.
intents.scale: Miners query distinct global BIN/IIN databases to check card token validity and bank routing.

intents.name: FRAUD_RISK
intents.description: Computes real-time behavioral fraud probability scores using device fingerprinting, IP geolocation, and transaction context.
intents.why: A risk score with no ground truth at query time; the label only arrives later.
intents.scale: Miners use different risk-engine APIs to evaluate IP geolocation and device fingerprinting.

intents.name: TRANSACTION_RISK
intents.description: Evaluates spending velocity, merchant categorization codes, and chargeback history to score transaction risk.
intents.why: Same shape as FRAUD_RISK: a forward-looking score.
intents.scale: Miners query different payment risk evaluation endpoints for chargeback probability scores.

intents.name: LLM_OUTPUT_EVALUATION
intents.description: Evaluates generative model responses against factual ground truth, citation fidelity, hallucination markers, and safety guardrails.
intents.why: Judging generative output against fidelity and safety is the definition of judgment.
intents.scale: 10 miners run 10 different judge LLMs.

intents.name: REGULATORY_FILING_MONITOR
intents.description: Parses statutory regulatory filings, 10-K/10-Q disclosures, and disclosure updates from financial oversight portals.
intents.why: A filing appeared on EDGAR or it did not.
intents.scale: Miners scrape different official financial oversight RSS feeds and registry APIs.

intents.name: CORPORATE_REGISTRY_LOOKUP
intents.description: Queries national business registers for incorporation status, registered agent details, and beneficial ownership filings.
intents.why: Registry record fields.
intents.scale: OpenCorporates aggregates 140+ global registries; miners query different jurisdictions.

intents.name: B2B_IDENTITY_ENRICHMENT
intents.description: Enriches business entity records with corporate tax IDs, headquarters addresses, executive listings, and domain validation.
intents.why: Firmographic fields are facts; entity resolution and coverage are judgment.
intents.scale: Miners query distinct B2B firmographic databases to cross-reference tax IDs and addresses.
intents.verifyNote: Firmographic databases are proprietary and disagree for the same company; there is no canonical public truth to converge on.

intents.name: CONTRACT_OBLIGATION_AUDIT
intents.description: Parses and verifies legal contract milestone deliverables, payment terms, and vendor performance commitments.
intents.why: Extracting obligations from prose; competent lawyers disagree on scope.
intents.scale: 10 miners use 10 different LLMs to extract milestone JSON schemas from legal text.

intents.name: DOCUMENT_AUTHENTICITY
intents.description: Validates digital certificate signatures, notarizations, tamper-evident seals, and document checksum integrity.
intents.why: PKI signature verifies mechanically; forgery assessment of the artifact does not.
intents.scale: Miners independently hash documents and verify cryptographic PKI signatures on-chain.
intents.verifyNote: Signature validity is a locally computed cryptographic check rather than a fetchable value, which the current fetch-based verification cannot express.

intents.name: MACRO_ECONOMIC_INDICATOR
intents.description: Aggregates released central bank interest rates, consumer price index (CPI) updates, and unemployment figures.
intents.why: Published statistic from a central bank or stat agency.
intents.scale: Miners query different federal reserve nodes, statistical agencies, and open finance endpoints.

intents.name: MEDIA_FORENSIC_VERIFY
intents.description: Detects AI deepfake artifacts, EXIF metadata manipulation, and generative audio/video synthesis in media uploads.
intents.why: Deepfake and manipulation assessment has no authoritative label.
intents.scale: Miners use distinct open-source deepfake detection models via Hugging Face.
intents.verifyNote: No authoritative public label to converge on, and the current evaluation pipeline is text-only, so images and audio cannot yet be scored.

intents.name: FX_NOW
intents.description: Provides real-time institutional foreign exchange mid-market rates, spreads, and currency conversion quotes.
intents.why: Mid-market rate, numeric tolerance, short TTL.
intents.scale: Miners query different liquidity feeds to calculate mid-market consensus.

intents.name: INVOICE_LEDGER_RECONCILE
intents.description: Performs automated 3-way matching between invoice line items, purchase orders, and receiving dock receipts.
intents.why: Exact matches reconcile mechanically; partial and fuzzy matches are judgment.
intents.scale: Miners execute double-entry balance checks against distinct ERP ledger endpoints.
intents.verifyNote: The match runs against a private company ledger with no public replica for a validator to reproduce.

intents.name: PURCHASE_ORDER_VERIFY
intents.description: Reconciles enterprise purchase orders with procurement approval workflows, vendor quotas, and budget allocations.
intents.why: PO fields match the ERP record.
intents.scale: Miners use open-source ERP endpoints to execute deterministic 3-way matching.

intents.name: VENDOR_VERIFY
intents.description: Audits vendor tax identifiers, compliance credentials, banking details, and sanctions list clearance.
intents.why: Registration status is a lookup; vendor risk is an assessment.
intents.scale: Miners check tax identifiers and sanctions lists using distinct firmographic API endpoints.

intents.name: URL_SAFE
intents.description: Checks target URLs against live threat feeds, DNS blocklists, phishing databases, and domain reputation monitors.
intents.why: Known-bad feed hit is a lookup; an unlisted URL requires inference.
intents.scale: Miners hit different DNS blocklists and threat feeds.
intents.verifyNote: Threat-feed verdicts drift and differ across engines and over time.

intents.name: EMAIL_SECURITY
intents.description: Verifies SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records, inspects header anomalies, and detects spoofing or malicious attachments.
intents.why: SPF/DKIM/DMARC are mechanical; phishing intent is judgment.
intents.scale: Miners independently query and parse DNS MX, SPF, and DMARC TXT records.

intents.name: MALWARE_DETECTION
intents.description: Scans file hashes and binaries against multi-engine antivirus definitions and sandbox behavioral detonation traces.
intents.why: Multi-engine consensus gives a usable label; novel samples need judgment.
intents.scale: Miners detonate hashes against different antivirus engines.
intents.verifyNote: Multi-engine detection counts drift over time and differ per engine set.

intents.name: THREAT_INTELLIGENCE
intents.description: Aggregates indicators of compromise (IOCs), malicious IP ranges, and adversary tactics from global security feeds.
intents.why: Feed aggregation is mechanical; relevance and severity are assessed.
intents.scale: Miners query different open-source threat intelligence platforms for IOC scores.

intents.name: SOCIAL_BOT_DETECTION
intents.description: Classifies social media accounts by post frequency anomalies, follower graph clusters, and coordinated inauthentic behavior.
intents.why: No authoritative bot label exists; it is an inference over behaviour.
intents.scale: Miners pass target profiles through different heuristic models (follower ratio, burst timing).

intents.name: TASK_EXECUTION_QUALITY
intents.description: Benchmarks automated job or agent execution outputs against gold-standard rubrics and expected schema constraints.
intents.why: Scored against rubrics; no single correct execution.
intents.scale: Miners use different evaluation models to score agent output against standard rubrics.

intents.name: REGRESSION_VERIFY
intents.description: Runs automated test suite executions to confirm backward compatibility across modified service APIs and libraries.
intents.why: Test runner produces a pass/fail set.
intents.scale: Miners execute headless test suites across different cloud CI runners.

intents.name: PRODUCT_AUTHENTICITY
intents.description: Validates product provenance, serial numbers, and manufacturer anti-counterfeit records against authorized registries.
intents.why: Registry match is a fact; authenticity assessment on the remainder is judgment.
intents.scale: Miners cross-reference barcode and serial checksums across different global open registries.
intents.verifyNote: Free registries cannot return a trustworthy "not registered", and GS1 is membership-gated.

intents.name: SHIP_RATE_ETA
intents.description: Calculates and verifies carrier shipping rates, service tiers, and estimated delivery dates for specified zip codes.
intents.why: Quoted rate is a fact; the ETA is a prediction.
intents.scale: Miners ping 10+ different courier calculators.
intents.verifyNote: Quoted rates are account-specific, so there is no single public rate.

intents.name: RETURN_POLICY_VERIFY
intents.description: Validates order return eligibility, restocking fees, and merchant policy constraints based on purchase timestamp and category.
intents.why: Policy text is retrievable; applying it to a case is interpretation.
intents.scale: Miners use different LLMs to parse a merchant's policy URL and extract constraints.
intents.verifyNote: Policies change without versioning and need LLM extraction, so there is no stable fact to reproduce.

intents.name: TRAVEL_TRANSIT_LOCK
intents.description: Verifies and confirms fare holds, ticket reservation guarantees, and transit seat locking mechanisms.
intents.why: A booking lock exists in the GDS or it does not.
intents.scale: Miners query different Global Distribution System endpoints to confirm PNR record locators.
intents.verifyNote: A fare hold exists inside one private GDS session with no public replica.

intents.name: FLIGHT_AVAILABILITY
intents.description: Queries real-time airline schedule networks, cabin seat inventories, and booking fare class statuses.
intents.why: Seat availability from the GDS.
intents.scale: Miners query different providers for seat inventories.
intents.verifyNote: Fare-class seat inventory is private and keyed.

intents.name: HOTEL_AVAILABILITY
intents.description: Confirms room inventory, nightly rates, amenities, and cancellation policies across hospitality property management systems.
intents.why: Room availability from the PMS.
intents.scale: Miners use different OTA aggregator APIs to confirm room availability.
intents.verifyNote: Inventory is private and no keyless public source exists.

intents.name: FARE_RULE_VERIFY
intents.description: Inspects fare terms, baggage allowances, cancellation penalties, and change fee stipulations for booked travel tickets.
intents.why: Rule text is retrievable; applying it to an itinerary is interpretation.
intents.scale: Miners query different travel aggregators to parse change fees and baggage allowances.
intents.verifyNote: Fare rules are session-specific and change per query.

intents.name: ROUTE_ETA
intents.description: Computes multimodal routing itineraries, live traffic transit times, and turn-by-turn arrival estimations.
intents.why: Scored as numeric agreement with routing-engine consensus.
intents.scale: Miners query different routing engines to output median transit time.

intents.name: CUSTOMER_TICKET_RESOLUTION
intents.description: Analyzes helpdesk support interactions, resolution accuracy, agent action compliance, and customer satisfaction outcomes.
intents.why: Resolution accuracy and CSAT reasoning are comparative.
intents.scale: Miners use different semantic evaluation LLMs to score ticket resolution accuracy.

intents.name: SLA_COMPLIANCE
intents.description: Measures operational response and resolution turnaround against contractually agreed service level agreements.
intents.why: Measured against a threshold in the APM ledger.
intents.scale: Miners query different APM dashboards for uptime telemetry.
intents.verifyNote: Measured against a private APM ledger, so the network would have to trust one party's data.

intents.name: VALIDATOR_PERFORMANCE_VERIFY
intents.description: Tracks consensus voting uptime, proposed block rates, slashing penalties, and staking APR for network validators.
intents.why: Uptime and attestation rates from consensus telemetry.
intents.scale: Miners query independent consensus layer block explorers to calculate uptime.

intents.name: GRID_POWER_PRICE
intents.description: Ingests real-time nodal locational marginal prices and day-ahead electricity spot rates from regional grid operators.
intents.why: Published ISO/RTO settlement price.
intents.scale: Miners query independent regional ISOs and grid telemetry dashboards directly.

intents.name: MINING_HASHPRICE_VERIFY
intents.description: Calculates proof-of-work mining revenue per unit of hashing power based on block rewards and network difficulty.
intents.why: Derived from observable pool and block-explorer data.
intents.scale: Miners query different mempool explorers and difficulty calculators.

intents.name: DATACENTER_TELEMETRY_VERIFY
intents.description: Audits rack power usage effectiveness (PUE), server thermal telemetry, and backup generator readiness metrics.
intents.why: Sensor readings from the BMS.
intents.scale: Miners query enterprise edge endpoints and standard open-source APM metrics.
intents.verifyNote: Readings come from a private building management system and are not publicly reproducible.

intents.name: SATELLITE_IMAGERY_ANALYSIS
intents.description: Processes multispectral satellite feeds for land use changes, crop vegetation indexes, and infrastructure monitoring.
intents.why: Open-ended interpretation of imagery.
intents.scale: Miners use different CV models to classify the same Sentinel/Landsat image.
intents.verifyNote: No authoritative public label to converge on, and the current evaluation pipeline is text-only, so imagery cannot yet be scored.

intents.name: SENSOR_TELEMETRY_VERIFY
intents.description: Validates edge sensor heartbeat signals, cryptographic payload integrity, and calibration threshold bounds.
intents.why: MQTT broker readings.
intents.scale: Miners subscribe to distinct IoT broker endpoints and evaluate payload HMAC signatures.

intents.name: LIVE_PORT_CONGESTION
intents.description: Measures container port vessel queue wait times, berth occupancy ratios, and dwell day averages.
intents.why: Vessel counts and dwell times are measured; 'congestion' is a derived assessment.
intents.scale: Miners query different open maritime tracking networks to count anchored vessel queues.
intents.verifyNote: Congestion is time-sensitive; two queries seconds apart differ.

intents.name: VESSEL_TELEMETRY_VERIFY
intents.description: Ingests maritime AIS transponder data to track vessel speed, draft, bunker fuel burn, and nautical headings.
intents.why: AIS position and heading.
intents.scale: Miners query diverse crowdsourced AIS aggregator hubs for ship coordinates and draft.

intents.name: WEATHER_FORECAST_VERIFY
intents.description: Reconciles localized Doppler radar feeds, barometric pressure, wind gusts, and severe weather alert bulletins.
intents.why: Forecast compared against subsequent observation.
intents.scale: Open-Meteo aggregates 15+ weather models; miners query different underlying models.

intents.name: PACKAGE_STATUS
intents.description: Tracks parcel checkpoint milestones, courier custody transfers, and delivery progress across logistics carriers.
intents.why: Carrier scan events.
intents.scale: Miners query different tracking aggregators covering 1,000+ couriers.
intents.verifyNote: Tracking lives in private carrier databases behind keyed aggregators.

intents.name: DELIVERY_WINDOW_VERIFY
intents.description: Confirms driver dispatch route scheduling, customer delivery appointment slots, and signature requirements.
intents.why: Committed window from the dispatch system.
intents.scale: Miners query distinct last-mile dispatch routing algorithms to confirm appointment slots.
intents.verifyNote: Committed windows live only in a private dispatch system.

intents.name: WAREHOUSE_INVENTORY
intents.description: Audits bin and pallet level stock counts, pick-and-pack allocations, and replenishment thresholds in fulfillment centers.
intents.why: Counts from the WMS.
intents.scale: Miners verify warehouse bin quantities via distinct WMS endpoint queries.
intents.verifyNote: Counts live only in a private WMS.

intents.name: CARRIER_SERVICEABILITY
intents.description: Evaluates freight and courier delivery coverage, weight limits, and hazardous material restrictions for target routes.
intents.why: Lane serviceable or not, from the routing matrix.
intents.scale: Miners query distinct courier rating matrices to confirm hazmat and weight limits.

intents.name: SHIPMENT_DELAY_RISK
intents.description: Assesses predictive delay risk based on customs processing times, port congestion, weather conditions, and transport nodes.
intents.why: Forward-looking risk over weather, congestion and customs; truth arrives later.
intents.scale: Miners use distinct risk models to weigh port congestion against weather delay factors.

intents.name: CURRENCY_EXCHANGE
intents.description: Calculates fiat currency conversion rates and mid-market spot pricing across global currency pairs.
intents.why: Spot exchange rate at timestamp within numeric tolerance band.
intents.scale: Miners query distinct FX liquidity providers and calculate median mid-market rate.

intents.name: CRYPTO_TRANSFER_VERIFY
intents.description: Verifies on-chain transaction status, gas fee burn, sender/recipient addresses, and block confirmations.
intents.why: Transaction inclusion and confirmation count are verified directly on-chain.
intents.scale: Miners query diverse archive RPC nodes to cross-verify transaction receipt status and events.

intents.name: SMART_CONTRACT_AUDIT
intents.description: Inspects bytecode and smart contract source code for reentrancy, access control, and integer overflows.
intents.why: Automated vulnerability patterns are mechanical; business logic flaws require semantic analysis.
intents.scale: Miners run distinct open-source static analyzers and automated formal verification suites.

intents.name: AIR_QUALITY_INDEX
intents.description: Aggregates particulate matter, ground ozone, and composite AQI metrics from monitoring stations.
intents.why: Sensor measurements of PM2.5, PM10, and ozone concentrations.
intents.scale: Miners cross-reference municipal air monitoring station telemetry and calibrated sensor APIs.

intents.name: THREAT_IP_REPUTATION
intents.description: Assesses malicious IP address risk scores, botnet associations, and brute-force history across threat registries.
intents.why: Blocklist presence is a deterministic lookup; composite confidence score is an inference.
intents.scale: Miners query diverse global IP threat feeds and aggregate historical abuse report counts.

intents.name: DNS_RECORD_LOOKUP
intents.description: Resolves and validates authoritative DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT) across global resolvers.
intents.why: Authoritative nameserver response for requested record type.
intents.scale: Miners query authoritative and anycast DNS resolvers to verify propagation and record parity.

intents.name: PORT_SCAN_AUDIT
intents.description: Identifies open network service ports, banner disclosures, and listening daemon protocols on specified hosts.
intents.why: TCP SYN/ACK handshake state or open UDP response is observable network truth.
intents.scale: Miners scan target endpoints using controlled SYN probes to confirm listening service ports.

intents.name: SERVER_UPTIME_MONITOR
intents.description: Monitors HTTP/HTTPS endpoint availability, handshake latency, and uptime status from multiple edge regions.
intents.why: HTTP response code and TCP latency from synthetic edge probes.
intents.scale: Miners execute concurrent HTTP GET requests from geo-distributed locations.

intents.name: API_HEALTH_CHECK
intents.description: Verifies REST/GraphQL API responsiveness, JSON schema payload structure, and HTTP status codes.
intents.why: Service payload validation and response code comparison against OpenAPI specification.
intents.scale: Miners execute automated schema conformance checks against public health endpoints.

intents.name: CLOUD_RESOURCE_USAGE
intents.description: Audits virtual machine and container compute utilization, memory pressure, and network throughput metrics.
intents.why: CPU, memory, and network telemetry counters exported by hypervisor metrics.
intents.scale: Miners query open Prometheus exporter metrics to verify real-time hardware telemetry.

intents.name: CREDIT_SCORE_VERIFY
intents.description: Validates consumer credit bureau score ranges, adverse factors, and debt-to-income benchmarks.
intents.why: Bureau numerical score is a lookup; credit risk tiering involves underwriting criteria.
intents.scale: Miners cross-reference credit bureau score bands across test scoring engines.

intents.name: LOAN_INTEREST_RATE_QUOTE
intents.description: Aggregates residential mortgage APRs, prime lending rates, and personal loan interest quotes.
intents.why: Published benchmark APRs from institutional lending matrices.
intents.scale: Miners scrape and parse published APR tables across licensed lenders.

intents.name: CRYPTO_YIELD_RATE
intents.description: Tracks annualized percentage yields, staking reward rates, and lending pool yields across DeFi protocols.
intents.why: Calculated from smart contract liquidity pools and staking emission contracts.
intents.scale: Miners query smart contract liquidity pools directly to calculate instantaneous lending APY.

intents.name: TOKEN_TOTAL_SUPPLY_VERIFY
intents.description: Verifies token circulating supply, burnt token balances, and total minted token counts on-chain.
intents.why: Calling totalSupply() on an ERC-20/SPL contract returns an exact integer.
intents.scale: Miners execute eth_call view functions against token contracts via independent archive nodes.

intents.name: ENTITY_EXTRACTION
intents.description: Extracts named entities (people, organizations, locations, dates) with character offsets from unstructured text.
intents.why: Standard entity spans are verifiable; disambiguation and novel entity types require judgment.
intents.scale: Miners run distinct open-source NER models to cross-verify entity span annotations.

intents.name: TEXT_SUMMARIZATION
intents.description: Generates concise, factual executive summaries capturing primary themes of long-form source documents.
intents.why: Multiple valid summaries exist; evaluation is inherently comparative.
intents.scale: Miners generate summaries using varied foundation LLMs evaluated via ROUGE, BERTScore, and LLM-as-judge.

intents.name: SENTIMENT_ANALYSIS
intents.description: Scores emotional valence, polarity, and subjective tone in textual messages.
intents.why: Binary polarity on clear text is objective; nuanced tone and sarcasm require interpretation.
intents.scale: Miners classify input text across diverse pre-trained sentiment models and aggregate distributions.

intents.name: LANGUAGE_TRANSLATION
intents.description: Translates multilingual text between language pairs preserving semantic intent and idiom.
intents.why: Fluency and phrasing vary; no single authoritative translation exists.
intents.scale: Miners translate across different neural machine translation models scored by BLEU and COMET.

intents.name: SPEECH_TO_TEXT
intents.description: Transcribes spoken audio into punctuated, timestamped text with speaker diarization.
intents.why: Acoustic signal has phonetic ground truth, but accents and noise introduce ambiguity.
intents.scale: Miners run varied Whisper checkpoints and compute Word Error Rate.

intents.name: TEXT_TO_SPEECH
intents.description: Synthesizes natural-sounding spoken voice from text input with adjustable emotion and cadence.
intents.why: Acoustic realism, prosody, and naturalness are perceptual judgments.
intents.scale: Miners synthesize audio and evaluate perceptual quality using NISQA and MOS estimators.

intents.name: IMAGE_CAPTIONING
intents.description: Generates descriptive, contextual captions describing the primary subjects and scenes in images.
intents.why: Salient objects and visual descriptions have multiple valid formulations.
intents.scale: Miners run distinct vision-language models evaluated with CIDEr and CLIP score.

intents.name: QUESTION_ANSWERING
intents.description: Answers open-domain and context-bounded queries with cited factual assertions and logical deductions.
intents.why: Factual premise is checkable against reference knowledge; completeness and phrasing require judgment.
intents.scale: Miners generate reasoning paths evaluated against authoritative ground truth documents via LLM judge.

intents.name: CHATBOT_CONVERSATION
intents.description: Maintains multi-turn conversational context, tone alignment, and empathetic response delivery.
intents.why: Conversational flow, persona adherence, and helpfulness are subjective.
intents.scale: Miners generate dialogue turns evaluated against persona rubrics and safety constraints.

intents.name: CODE_GENERATION
intents.description: Generates executable, type-safe code snippets and algorithms meeting specified functional specifications.
intents.why: Compilation and unit tests are deterministic; style and architecture are judgment.
intents.scale: Miners generate candidate implementations executed in sandboxes against unit test suites.
intents.method: Unit Test Pass Rate + LLM Review

intents.name: TEXT_CLASSIFICATION
intents.description: Assigns predefined category tags and topic hierarchies to incoming text documents.
intents.why: Clear category matches are mechanical; boundary cases require probabilistic inference.
intents.scale: Miners run zero-shot classification pipelines and vote on label distributions.

intents.name: GRAMMAR_SPELL_CHECK
intents.description: Detects typographical, orthographic, punctuation, and grammatical errors with correction offsets.
intents.why: Lexicon lookup and formal grammatical rules are deterministically verifiable.
intents.scale: Miners evaluate text against open-source linguistic rule sets.

intents.name: KEYWORD_EXTRACTION
intents.description: Extracts representative topical keywords, keyphrases, and n-grams from body text.
intents.why: Term frequency is mechanical; conceptual relevance ranking is judgment.
intents.scale: Miners run distinct keyphrase algorithms and compute rank intersection.

intents.name: PLAGIARISM_DETECTION
intents.description: Detects verbatim duplication, disguised paraphrasing, and uncredited citations across corpus databases.
intents.why: N-gram fingerprint matching is mechanical; paraphrasing and attribution require judgment.
intents.scale: Miners generate min-hash fingerprints and query web index corpora to calculate overlap.

intents.name: SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY
intents.description: Calculates cosine similarity and semantic relatedness between pairs of sentences.
intents.why: Cosine similarity between normalized embedding vectors is an exact calculation.
intents.scale: Miners generate vectors using standard reference models and compute cosine products.

intents.name: EMBEDDING_GENERATION
intents.description: Transforms text into standardized high-dimensional vector embeddings for retrieval systems.
intents.why: A fixed model with a deterministic forward pass returns invariant vectors.
intents.scale: Miners run the exact model weights to confirm output vectors within floating-point epsilon.

intents.name: LANGUAGE_GENERATION
intents.description: Query asks about how language generation works as a capability or technique, or requests free-form natural-language output from a described prompt. Prefer CHAT_COMPLETION for ordinary conversational questions.

intents.name: CHAT_COMPLETION
intents.description: General knowledge, reasoning, explanation, or conversational question answerable directly without live data, external sources, or specialized tooling. This is the default/general-purpose intent when nothing more specific clearly fits — e.g. 'explain what X does.'

intents.name: TEXT_GENERATION
intents.description: Query asks for free-form written output for a described task — drafting, rewriting, summarising or composing text. Prefer CHAT_COMPLETION when the user simply wants an answer rather than produced text.

intents.name: WEATHER_CHECK
intents.description: Query names a specific, resolvable location (city, region, coordinates) AND asks about CURRENT atmospheric/weather conditions there (e.g. current temperature). A location mentioned only in passing in an unrelated question does not qualify.

intents.name: STORM_ALERT
intents.description: Query names a specific, resolvable location and asks specifically about active or upcoming storm systems, high winds, or disruption risk from severe weather there — not general current conditions.

intents.name: WEATHER_FORECAST
intents.description: Query names a specific, resolvable location and asks for FUTURE weather conditions over a stated time window (e.g. 'next 24 hours'), not current conditions.

intents.name: GAME_RESULT
intents.description: Query names a specific completed sports fixture or competition and asks for its final outcome or winner. Distinct from an in-progress or live score, which is SPORTS_SCORE.

intents.name: WALLET_BALANCE_CHECK
intents.description: Query names a specific blockchain address or ENS name and asks for its current native-coin or token balance on a named chain. A question that merely mentions a wallet without asking what it holds does not qualify.

intents.name: FRAUD_DETECTION
intents.description: Query asks how likely a specific entity, transaction or action is to be fraudulent.

intents.name: TASK_COMPLETION
intents.description: Query asks about what makes an AI agent effective at completing multi-step tasks, or is itself a request to complete a defined multi-step task end-to-end.

intents.name: AGENT_TASK
intents.description: Query asks about autonomous AI agent behavior specifically (tool use, taking actions, multi-step autonomy) as distinct from a standard chatbot, or is itself a request requiring autonomous multi-step action.

intents.name: WEB_SEARCH
intents.description: Query needs current, live, or externally-sourced information not reliably answerable from static/training knowledge — general 'what is the current price of Bitcoin' questions that need up-to-date grounding.

intents.name: TWITTER_SEARCH
intents.description: Query asks to search posts, accounts or discussion on X/Twitter specifically. A question that merely mentions Twitter as a topic does not qualify — the user must want results from the platform.

intents.name: NEWS_SEARCH
intents.description: Query asks for news articles or coverage matching a topic, entity or time period. Prefer NEWS_HEADLINES when the user wants a headline list rather than article results.

intents.name: RESEARCH_SYNTHESIS
intents.description: Query asks to gather findings across multiple sources and synthesise them into a combined answer or summary, rather than returning a single fact or a list of links.

intents.name: FACT_CHECK
intents.description: Query supplies a specific claim or statement and asks whether it is true, with supporting evidence. A general knowledge question is CHAT_COMPLETION — this intent requires a checkable claim.

intents.name: TEXT_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK
intents.description: Query supplies a block of text and asks whether it is genuine, original, or machine-generated. Where the user explicitly asks about AI authorship, prefer AI_TEXT_DETECTION.

intents.name: AI_TEXT_DETECTION
intents.description: Query provides a specific block of text and asks whether it was written by an AI or a human. The user must supply actual text content to analyze — a question that merely asks about AI detection conceptually (without providing text to analyze) is not this intent.

intents.name: CONTENT_VERIFICATION
intents.description: Query asks whether a specific piece of supplied content is genuine and unaltered, covering provenance and integrity generally rather than media forensics specifically.

intents.name: DEEPFAKE_DETECTION
intents.description: Query includes an actual image or video URL/reference and specifically asks whether it is a deepfake or whether a face/person in it has been synthetically generated or swapped. Requires real attached media — the word 'deepfake' alone with no media reference does not qualify.

intents.name: MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK
intents.description: Query includes an actual image or video URL/reference and asks broadly whether it is authentic, real, or AI-generated. Words like 'authentic,' 'real,' 'validity,' or 'genuine' alone, with no actual media attached, do NOT qualify.

intents.name: IMAGE_VERIFICATION
intents.description: Query includes an actual image URL/reference and asks whether it has been digitally manipulated, edited, or spliced (distinct from asking if it's AI-generated outright — that's MEDIA_AUTHENTICITY_CHECK). Requires real attached media.

intents.name: VIDEO_VERIFICATION
intents.description: Query references an actual video file or URL and asks to verify its authenticity, origin, or whether it has been edited/deepfaked. The mere word 'video' in an unrelated question does not qualify — requires a real attached video.

intents.name: GAS_PRICE
intents.description: Query asks for the current or recent transaction fee level on a named blockchain network. Distinct from the price of that chain's token, which is CRYPTO_PRICE.

intents.name: CONTENT_MODERATION
intents.description: Query is itself asking to classify, flag, or moderate a specific piece of provided content, OR asks how automated content moderation works as a method/technique — not merely a question that mentions moderation as an unrelated concept.

intents.name: STOCK_PRICE
intents.description: Query names a listed equity or ticker and asks for its current or historical share price. A company mentioned in passing does not qualify.

intents.name: CRYPTO_PRICE
intents.description: Query names a cryptocurrency asset and asks for its current or historical price. Prefer FINANCIAL_DATA for broader market or fundamentals questions.

intents.name: FINANCIAL_DATA
intents.description: Query asks for market data, company fundamentals, or financial statistics beyond a single quoted price.

intents.name: ACADEMIC_SEARCH
intents.description: Query asks to search scholarly papers, journals or academic literature specifically, rather than the general web.

intents.name: ONCHAIN_TX_LOOKUP
intents.description: Query supplies a transaction hash or names a specific on-chain transaction and asks for its details, status or effects. Requires an actual transaction reference, not a general question about how transactions work.

intents.name: TOKEN_HOLDER_COUNT
intents.description: Query names a specific token or contract address and asks how many distinct addresses hold it. Not a request for the token's price, supply or market data.

intents.name: TVL_LOOKUP
intents.description: Query names a specific DeFi protocol, pool or chain and asks for the total value locked in it. Distinct from a token's market capitalisation.

intents.name: URL_SCAN
intents.description: Query supplies a URL and asks for it to be scanned and judged safe or unsafe.

intents.name: RESEARCH_QUERY
intents.description: Query asks a research question and expects an answer supported by citations to sources.

intents.name: IP_GEOLOCATION
intents.description: Query supplies an IP address and asks where it is located geographically. For abuse history, use IP_REPUTATION.

intents.name: NEWS_HEADLINES
intents.description: Query asks for current news headlines for a topic or region, as a list rather than full articles.

intents.name: CVE_LOOKUP
intents.description: Query supplies a CVE identifier and asks for its details, severity or affected versions.

intents.name: TELEGRAPH_KNOWLEDGE
intents.description: Query asks about Telegraph, Telegraph protocol, its products, or ecosystem — including Alexandria (flagship intelligence layer), the Explorer (leaderboard, live feed, signal search), Hackathon, WASM/miner registration, intents, the Miner YAML Registry (integrate.telegraphprotocol.com), current miners or their details, and any applications built on Telegraph (TruthWire, TrustFilter, ScholarGuard, ReviewRadar). Also covers protocol fundamentals like tokenomics, architecture, documentation, earning, and how the system works. Also covers any question where the user addresses the assistant directly as "you" (e.g. "what can you do", "who are you", "how can I use you") — the assistant is Telegraph. Use this for ANY question related to Telegraph, its products, platforms, ecosystem, or the assistant itself, rather than routing to general CHAT_COMPLETION or WEB_SEARCH.

intents.name: SSL_VERIFICATION
intents.description: Query supplies a hostname or domain and asks about its TLS/SSL certificate, chain or configuration.

intents.name: CONTENT_EXTRACTION
intents.description: Query supplies unstructured content and asks for specific structured fields to be pulled out of it.

intents.name: SPORTS_SCORE
intents.description: Query names a specific sports fixture, team or competition and asks for the current or most recent score. Distinct from asking who ultimately won a finished event, which is GAME_RESULT.

ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.name: Exchange
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.summary: An autonomous listings desk that buys contract audit, contributor authenticity, holder concentration and sanctions exposure in parallel, and returns a signed listing risk memo with a cost line at the bottom.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.problem: Listing reviews take weeks of analyst time, surveillance is bought per seat from a single in-house model, and counterparty checks mean exposing your book.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.outcome: An exchange desk that runs on bought intelligence: every listing, alert and counterparty decision arrives with the receipts that informed it and a cost line.

examples.title: The autonomous listings desk
examples.body: A token listing application arrives. An agent fires parallel paid requests through Telegraph: contract audit, commit history and contributor authenticity, holder concentration, sanctions exposure on treasury addresses, and bot-versus-human analysis of the project's social following. The output is a signed listing risk memo with a verification hash and a cost line at the bottom. Run it against a real pending listing candidate and print the total: a few dollars and ninety seconds, against weeks of analyst time.
examples.output: Signed listing risk memo with a cost line

examples.title: Surveillance that only bills when it finds something
examples.body: A market-integrity agent buys order-book anomaly detection continuously through Telegraph rather than running one in-house model. Each request routes to the miner currently ranked best for it, and the venue pays per request instead of per seat. Then invert it: the surveillance agent republishes its consolidated alert feed as a miner, so compliance agents at other venues can buy from it.
examples.output: A ranked alert feed, resold as a miner

examples.title: The solvency handshake
examples.body: Two exchange agents verify each other before extending counterparty credit. Each buys a solvency attestation on the other through Telegraph, without either book being exposed. The verification and the cross-agent purchase run fully on testnet. The credit decision that follows needs mainnet, and a counterparty willing to be the other side.
examples.output: Mutual solvency check before credit

ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.name: Stablecoin
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.summary: An agent fleet with a real expense ledger, compliance screening attached to the payment itself as a proof, and a machine that opens a vault, borrows, spends on intelligence, earns as a miner and repays.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.problem: Agent spending looks nothing like a card payment or a wire, so no existing reporting, compliance or treasury tooling captures it.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.outcome: Money infrastructure for machines: agents that pay, screen, borrow and rebalance on verified evidence, with every settlement countable on chain.

examples.title: The agent expense ledger
examples.body: A fleet of agents runs for the full 30 days, paying for every request, with a dashboard showing burn per intelligence category, cost per completed task, and automated top-up when a wallet runs low. The headline number is settlement count, and it is genuine: tens of thousands of individual payments executed. Agent spending is a transaction class that no existing reporting captures, because it looks nothing like a card payment or a wire.
examples.output: Expense ledger: burn per category, cost per task

examples.title: Compliance attached to the payment itself
examples.body: Before an agent pays a miner, it buys a screening request: sanctions status, address risk score, jurisdiction eligibility. The verified result is attached to the payment as a proof, so the payment carries its own defensibility. Machine-to-machine Travel Rule mechanics, implemented rather than described.
examples.output: A payment that carries its own compliance proof

examples.title: Treasury agents choosing on evidence
examples.body: An autonomous treasury agent buys reserve-quality and cross-chain liquidity-depth answers through Telegraph, then rebalances on what it learns. The buying and the decision logic are real and auditable now. The rebalance runs against live market data as a simulation until mainnet, and the demo says so on screen.
examples.output: Evidence-backed rebalance, simulated until mainnet

examples.title: Machine-settled trade finance
examples.body: An agent releases payment against a shipment only after buying verified bill-of-lading, vessel position and customs-clearance answers through Telegraph. The conditional logic, the verification and the release trigger all run for real on testnet. The corridor economics arrive with mainnet.
examples.output: Payment released only against verified shipment facts

examples.title: Edge agents that pay when they can reach the network
examples.body: Agents running on cheap local hardware in low-connectivity conditions queue their requests, buy in a burst when a connection appears, and cache the verified answers locally. This proves the network works outside a data centre, and nothing about it needs mainnet to be true.
examples.output: Offline-first agent with cached verified answers

examples.title: Gold-collateralised agent wallets
examples.body: An agent funds its intelligence budget from a tokenised gold position rather than a cash balance, converting only what it spends. The conversion and spend path are built end to end; the collateral is test-denominated until mainnet. Pairs with the mining examples in Mission 06.
examples.output: Intelligence budget funded from tokenised gold

examples.title: A machine with a balance sheet
examples.body: An agent opens a collateralised vault, borrows, spends on intelligence, earns by reselling a composite answer as a miner, and repays. Full cycle, fully built, running on testnet collateral. Autonomous credit is the most under-built idea in the agent economy and this demonstrates the whole mechanism. Label the denomination everywhere the word "earned" appears on screen.
examples.output: Borrow, spend, earn and repay, all by one agent

examples.title: Collateral quality bought per request
examples.body: Risk parameters for real-world-asset collateral are set today by committee and vendor data. Instead, an agent buys verified answers on collateral quality through Telegraph, and the resulting parameter change is proposed on-chain with every input receipted. The analysis is real work product regardless of which network settled it.
examples.output: On-chain parameter proposal with every input receipted

examples.title: A treasury that shows its working
examples.body: A governance execution agent buys verified analysis before rebalancing or voting, and attaches the receipts to the proposal. Voters audit not just the decision but what the machine paid to inform it, and which inputs disagreed.
examples.output: Governance proposal with its receipts attached

ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.name: Asset Management
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.summary: Open research with every input priced and provable, index rebalancing with receipts on liquidity and float, and a daily holdings proof an investor agent can verify without the issuer.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.problem: Research notes and index methodologies assert numbers nobody can trace, private marks are opinions until someone transacts, and holdings are taken on faith.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.outcome: Research, indices and funds where every figure carries a receipt an investor's own agent can check.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.context: Thematic investment managers publish their theses in public, hold blockchain tokens directly, and their entire edge is research nobody else has done yet. What none of them have is a way to prove where a number in a research note came from, which is the one thing that separates a thesis from an assertion.

buyers.context: Disruptive innovation across public and private markets, an open research model that publishes its assumptions and invites people to attack them, and a venture book holding private companies.

examples.title: Open research with the inputs attached
examples.body: ARK publishes its models and asks to be argued with, which only works if a reader can get at the numbers underneath. An agent buys the verified inputs behind each assumption in a forecast - unit shipments, cost curves, adoption counts, capacity additions - through Telegraph, and attaches a receipt to every one. The model stays open and every figure in it becomes checkable without taking the author's word for the source.
examples.output: An open model with a receipt on every input

examples.title: A defensible mark on the venture book
examples.body: Private holdings are the hardest thing any of these firms carry, because the mark is an opinion until someone transacts. An agent buys secondary transaction comparables, funding round evidence, hiring velocity and product shipping signals through Telegraph, and produces a mark with every input priced and provable. A quarterly valuation nobody can reconstruct becomes one anybody can.
examples.output: A private mark anyone can reconstruct

examples.title: Forecast accountability, scored by machines
examples.body: Long-horizon public forecasts are almost never graded, because whoever grades them is accused of picking the scoring. An agent tracks each published forecast against verified outcomes as they arrive, buying corroborating evidence per checkpoint through Telegraph, and publishes a running scorecard nobody controls. This only appeals to a firm confident enough to invite the scrutiny, which narrows the audience to roughly one.
examples.output: A running forecast scorecard nobody controls

examples.title: The thematic screener that buys evidence
examples.body: An agent works a theme - robotics, nuclear, AI infrastructure - and buys hiring velocity, patent filings, permit applications, shipment records and supply-chain mentions through Telegraph, then ranks companies by observed activity rather than by press release. Every name in the ranking carries a receipt for why it is there. A screen built this way can be handed to a client with its sources attached, which is not true of any screen built today.
examples.output: A ranked screen with sources attached

examples.title: A token income statement
examples.body: An agent buys verified protocol revenue, active paying address counts, and wash-activity detection through Telegraph, and assembles the result into something an equity analyst can read. Analysts currently reconcile three dashboards that disagree with each other and pick one. Here every line traces to a ranked miner that was paid and scored on whether it was right.
examples.output: A token income statement an analyst can read

examples.title: Tokenized fund NAV with the proof attached
examples.body: An agent computes and publishes NAV for a tokenized fund, buying verified pricing and holdings attestations, and posts the value on-chain with its inputs provable. The calculation and the proof run now; doing it for a live fund is mainnet.
examples.output: An on-chain NAV with provable inputs

examples.title: Index rebalancing with receipts
examples.body: Before each rebalance, an agent buys verified liquidity depth, free float, custody eligibility and venue integrity answers for every candidate constituent. The rebalance publishes with each input priced and proved. Index methodology stops being an assertion in a PDF and becomes something an investor's own agent can check.
examples.output: A rebalance published with its receipts

examples.title: The fake volume screen
examples.body: Exchange-reported volume is the weakest number in the industry and it drives inclusion decisions worth real money. Before an asset enters an index, agents buy verified volume-authenticity assessments through Telegraph and compare them against what the venue claims. The gap is the finding.
examples.output: The gap between reported and verified volume

examples.title: The index as a miner
examples.body: Publish index values and constituent weights as a paid answer that other agents buy: funds, structured product issuers, on-chain protocols needing a reference price. Index licensing is already a real business sold by annual contract. This version sells it per request, to machines, with the methodology provable on every call.
examples.output: Index values sold per request

examples.title: Daily proof of holdings
examples.body: An agent buys custody attestations and publishes a daily holdings proof any investor's agent can verify independently, without trusting the issuer and without waiting on an auditor's calendar. For a product whose entire premise is that the assets are there, an attestation nobody has to take on faith is the product.
examples.output: A daily holdings proof

examples.title: Staking yield priced against verified risk
examples.body: For staking products, an agent buys validator uptime, performance, commission changes and slashing history through Telegraph, then prices the risk against the advertised yield. That risk is currently accepted on the word of the operator collecting the fee.
examples.output: Yield priced against verified validator risk

examples.title: The investor agent that does its own diligence
examples.body: Flip the direction. A prospective investor's agent buys product structure, counterparty exposure, fee drag and tracking-error answers before allocating anywhere. Issuer agent and investor agent both on the network, neither taking the other's word. The diligence runs now; the allocation is mainnet.
examples.output: Investor-side diligence before allocating

ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.name: Web3 Native and DeFi
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.sector: Onchain traders, conditional contracts, whitehat security
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.summary: A sniper that buys bytecode and drainer analysis before committing capital, two agents settling a conditional escrow that resolves itself, and a bug bounty paid to the machine that proved the bug.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.problem: Traders buy into honeypots, conditional contracts resolve on trusted humans, and bug bounties wait on manual triage.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.outcome: Spectacle builds that prove the machine economy in public: agents that insure their own trades, settle their own agreements, and get paid for the bugs they prove.
ONCHAIN_METRIC_VERIFY.context: The spectacle use cases, designed for maximum virality on tech and crypto social media. They prove the machine economy to crypto-native and developer audiences.

buyers.generic: Onchain traders and whitehat security teams

examples.title: The rug-proof memecoin sniper
examples.body: An agent scans the mempool for new token contract deployments. Before committing capital, it fires paid requests through Telegraph for bytecode deconstruction, drainer logic detection, and wash-trading analysis, each routed to the miner ranked best for it. If the verdict comes back malicious, the agent aborts. If safe, it buys. Run a live stream of a bot dodging five honeypots and executing on the sixth, with the Telegraph spend panel showing the exact cost of the execution insurance.
examples.output: Five honeypots dodged, execution on the sixth

examples.title: The self-settling conditional escrow
examples.body: Two autonomous agents lock funds in an escrow contract whose release depends on a real-world event, for example a delivery confirmed or a launch completed. The contract is hardcoded to buy an event outcome resolution from Telegraph: the request routes to the miner ranked best for event outcomes, and the verified answer, with its receipt, releases the funds to the right agent. Machines agreeing terms, verifying reality, and settling funds without a human in the loop. The contract logic and verification execute on testnet; the real-world payout denomination waits for mainnet.
examples.output: An escrow that settles itself on a verified outcome

examples.title: The autonomous bug bounty hunter
examples.body: An agent continuously crawls live smart contracts for vulnerabilities. When it finds one, it buys a vulnerability triage and exploit proof verification from Telegraph miners. The verified proof automatically triggers a payout from an on-chain bug bounty vault directly to the agent's wallet. A machine that hacks, proves it, and gets paid. The vulnerability verification is real today; the bounty payout is simulated on Sepolia.
examples.output: A bounty paid to the machine that proved the bug
